library.title: Programming with Scratch
library.summary: Your first programming language: building scripts from blocks in Scratch, with events, sequence, coordinates, loops, selection, variables, broadcasts, My Blocks and simulations, then planning, building and testing your own game.
learn: The Scratch window: stage, sprites, blocks palette and scripts area
Events and sequence, motion and x/y coordinates, costumes and animation
Loops (iteration) and if/if-else (selection) with sensing blocks
Variables, data types (number, text, true/false) and operators
Broadcasts, and abstraction with My Blocks and inputs (a bridge to functions and parameters)
Simulations: how changing a variable in a model changes the outcome
Debugging, and developing a game for a real user in cycles of plan, develop, test and refine (new NI curriculum links S1, S4, S7, C1, C3, C4)

library.title: Spreadsheets
library.summary: Using Microsoft Excel to store, calculate and present data: formulas, functions, cell references, charts and 'what if' models.
learn: What spreadsheets are for, and cells, rows, columns and ranges
Data types and formatting
Writing formulas and using functions such as SUM, AVERAGE, IF and COUNTIF
Relative and absolute cell references
Sorting, filtering, conditional formatting and charts
Building and testing a 'what if' model

library.title: Under the Hood
library.summary: What happens inside a computer: input, output, storage and memory devices, the CPU, the codebreakers of Bletchley Park, and how computers use binary.
learn: Input, output, storage and memory devices
The central processing unit (CPU)
Enigma, Lorenz, Colossus and the Manchester Baby
Decimal and binary numbers
Bits, bytes, kilobytes and megabytes

library.title: Designing for Users: UX and Accessibility
library.summary: How designers put users first: finding out what people need, writing user stories, following usability principles, sketching wireframes and prototypes, designing for accessibility (WCAG) and inclusion, testing with real users and improving in cycles.
learn: What user-centred design is, and why asking who a design works for matters as much as whether it works
How to find out user needs with interviews, surveys and observation, and sum them up in personas
How to write user stories and acceptance criteria
Usability principles, wireframes and prototypes, and how abstraction helps
Accessibility, the WCAG guidelines and the POUR principles, and avoiding bias with inclusive design
How to test with users (think-aloud and A/B tests) and improve a design
Development cycles: waterfall compared with iterative and agile approaches

library.title: Web Design
library.summary: Building web pages with HTML: how websites work, page structure, the tags you use, and styling with CSS.
learn: What HTML is, and the first website
Good and bad website design, and navigation
How a browser knows what to display
Page structure and HTML tags
Styling tags and CSS selectors
